evals.name: accounts-data-page
evals.prompt: An Arc app has generated proxies `AllAccounts` (observable query: name, balance, id) and `CreateAccount` (command with a name property), and a `CreateAccountDialog` already exists. Write the React `AccountsPage` with a table of name and balance and an 'Add account' toolbar action that opens the dialog. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A DataPage with title, query, emptyMessage and dataKey, columns inside DataPage.Columns, a MenuItem with command (not onClick) and an icon component, and a useDialog wrapper rendered once; imports from subpaths.
assertions: Imports DataPage, Column and MenuItem from the subpath '@cratis/components/DataPage', not from the root '@cratis/components'.
Passes the proxy to DataPage's query prop with title and emptyMessage, and does not pre-fetch rows and pass an array.
Places columns in <DataPage.Columns> and the action in <DataPage.MenuItems> as a MenuItem using the command prop rather than onClick.
Uses useDialog from '@cratis/arc.react/dialogs' and renders the returned wrapper component once in the tree.

evals.name: command-dialog-binding
evals.prompt: Write a `CreateAccountDialog` React component for an Arc app that runs the generated `CreateAccount` command (property `name`), closing with an OK result on success and Cancelled on cancel. A teammate suggests using a native <input> for the name field. Reply with the code and your view of that suggestion.
evals.expected_output: A CommandDialog with an InputTextField bound through a value accessor, closing via useDialogContext; the native input is rejected since it is not bound to the command so validation never reruns and submit stays disabled.
assertions: Builds the dialog on CommandDialog from '@cratis/components/CommandDialog' with command, title, onSuccess and onCancel.
Binds the name with a CommandForm field such as InputTextField using a value accessor like c => c.name and a title prop.
Closes the dialog through useDialogContext's closeDialog with DialogResult.Ok and DialogResult.Cancelled.
Rejects a raw native input or Common TextInput because it is not bound to the command, so validation never re-runs and the submit button stays disabled.

evals.name: confirm-and-busy
evals.prompt: On an Arc React page the Delete action should ask the user to confirm (it is destructive) and then show a busy indicator during a slow export. The developer plans window.confirm and a hand-written Yes/No dialog. How should this be done? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Register ConfirmationDialog and BusyIndicatorDialog once at the app root via DialogComponents and raise them with useConfirmationDialog and useBusyIndicator; destructive uses DialogInitialFocus.Cancel; pair showBusy with a close in a finally.
assertions: Recommends useConfirmationDialog instead of window.confirm or a hand-rolled Yes/No dialog.
Says ConfirmationDialog and BusyIndicatorDialog are registered once at the app root through DialogComponents.
Says a destructive dialog should use DialogInitialFocus.Cancel because Confirm is the default.
Says showBusy() must be paired with a close in a finally block.

evals.name: value-without-origin
evals.prompt: The designer wants the Accounts page to show an 'Owner email' column, but neither the `AllAccounts` read model nor any other proxy has that property. A teammate proposes fetching a second query on the client and joining it, or adding an `ownerEmail` property to the generated TypeScript proxy by hand. What do you do? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Do not fake it on the client or edit the generated proxy; it is a gap in the backend or model, so add the property to the read model first (or the .play model when it exists) and rebuild to regenerate proxies.
assertions: Refuses to compute the value from another query on the client.
Refuses to edit the generated proxy because it is marked DO NOT EDIT and is regenerated from the C# source.
Says a value with no origin is a gap in the backend or model and the property must be added to the read model first (or the .play model where one exists).
Says to rebuild so the TypeScript proxies are regenerated.

evals.name: acquisition-outcome-feedback
evals.prompt: An Accounts page executes a command outside a dialog. A validator can refuse it, or Provide() can return an explicit ValidationResult when acquisition yields no usable facts. One result has reason dependencyUnavailable and a diagnostic message naming backend internals. A teammate wants all invalid results displayed verbatim as field errors, or matched by English message text. Explain the correct client and backend responsibilities. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Both outcomes use validationResults; branch on flags and reason/reasonDetail, show safe copy for non-rule diagnostics, and use response only on success. Validators own refusals when facts exist; Provide only short-circuits failed acquisition and Handle does not duplicate validation.
assertions: Explains that validator refusals and explicit acquisition outcomes from Provide share validationResults, rather than a success response.
Branches on authorization, validity and exceptions, then reason/reasonDetail, never raw message text, and uses response only after success.
Distinguishes dependencyUnavailable from an authored rule refusal and selects safe application feedback instead of rendering diagnostic text as a field error.
Keeps business refusals in validators when usable facts exist, permits Provide to short-circuit only when acquisition yields nothing usable, and does not move duplicate validation into Handle.

evals.name: committed-menu-selection
evals.prompt: An Accounts DataPage has single-row selection and an Edit action. After the query replaces or removes a row, a controlled selection leaves stale details open. Show how to use a typed DataPage.MenuItem<AccountSummary> action and disabled predicate, and explain how the controlled selection should follow the query. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Typed callbacks receive the committed DataPageSelection discriminated union; single selection uses selectedItem and multiple selection uses readonly selectedItems. Use dataKey for replacement identity and accept event.value, including null on removal.
assertions: Uses an explicit MenuItem row generic rather than claiming JSX infers it from the parent DataPage.
Treats command and disabled callbacks as receiving the immutable committed selection, not a click event, and narrows selectionMode before reading selectedItem or selectedItems.
Explains that disabled and disableOnUnselected prevent action dispatch, while zero-argument commands remain valid.
Reconciles single selection by dataKey, or reference without one, and updates controlled state from onSelectionChange event.value, including null when the row disappears.

evals.name: whole-dataset-search
evals.prompt: Our paged Accounts DataPage has globalFilterFields but search only finds rows on the loaded page. We need whole-dataset search and sorting. A teammate says adding serverQuery automatically makes the backend understand search. Explain the real contract, including search callbacks, empty copy and paging behavior. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Default search/filter/sort is loaded-page-only. The caller maps DataTableServerQueryState into actual backend arguments through mapQueryArguments; serverQuery disables local processing, debounces text and resets paging when effective arguments change.
assertions: States that default search, filtering and sorting operate on the loaded page rather than the whole dataset.

Describes DataTableServerQuery<TArguments> with mapQueryArguments(state, baseArguments), optional debounceMs and state fields globalFilter, filters and sort, with types exported from @cratis/components/DataTables.

Requires backend query semantics for the mapped arguments rather than claiming serverQuery creates search automatically, and explains local processing is disabled and paging resets on effective argument changes.
Mentions onGlobalFilterChange, filteredEmptyMessage, and that text search is debounced while filters and sorting apply immediately.

evals.name: raw-validation-helper-gap
evals.prompt: A CommandDialog can receive validatorFailed, concurrencyViolation, constraintViolation or frameworkFailure results whose messages contain developer diagnostics. Does CommandForm or toastCommandResult sanitize those messages? Is onValidationFailure alone enough to prevent exposure? Recommend a safe approach. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Neither helper sanitizes validation diagnostics: CommandForm renders raw messages and toastCommandResult joins them. Own feedback by reason/reasonDetail, suppress built-in form errors when necessary, and never expose exception details.
assertions: Explicitly rejects the claim that CommandDialog, CommandForm or toastCommandResult sanitizes non-rule validation diagnostics.
Explains CommandForm's raw inline/summary rendering and toastCommandResult's joining of raw validation messages.
Uses application-owned feedback selected by reason/reasonDetail and showErrors={false} where necessary; onValidationFailure alone does not suppress built-in display.
Keeps exceptionMessages and exceptionStackTrace out of user-facing output and does not treat every invalid result as an authored field error.
